checks.details: javac --release 17 -Xlint:all exited 0; emitted class major version 61.
Witness extracted from positional tuple API, not parsed from a display string.
Exactly three rows mapped injectively to exactly two keys; nontrivial generated CNF observed.
Same four-bit model with noOverflow=true excludes the overflowing instance.

A fixed three-bit model has one Record, Key and Val, a ternary link and flag=1 or flag=2. A4Solution.next() yields both semantically distinct flag values, then UNSAT. Two next calls; cap=3 not reached. Both instances preserve [Record$0, Key$0, Val$0] in their declared tuple positions.

Javadoc -private -Xdoclint:all exited 0 without warnings after all explicit members were documented. Every authored method is at most 30 source lines including its signature and body, excluding Javadoc.

interpretation: The supplied jar can be embedded through a small Java17-only API adapter on Windows amd64 with bundled SAT4J.
Satisfiable and unsatisfiable results and typed witness tuples are available through the public API.

The incremental API supports bounded next-instance browsing. Instance order and atom labels are solver artifacts; this test establishes finite exhaustion only for its fixed tiny model, not exhaustive business-scenario coverage. Ordered n-ary tuple positions must remain intact in any future viewer.
No visualizer or AI provider was implemented or called. The new evidence can support a later instance viewer; AI prose must remain separate untrusted annotation tied to the selected instance.
Alloy integer bitwidth and noOverflow materially change admissible executions. Neither wraparound nor overflow-instance exclusion is a PostgreSQL error model.
SQLolla must reserve sufficient arithmetic/cardinality width and encode SQL range errors separately; setting noOverflow=true alone can hide a desired counterexample.
These tiny probes establish API connectivity, not database semantic preservation, solver completeness for a future encoding, production capacity or portable release readiness.
process_and_isolation_gaps: Probe uses fixed authored models and no public service. An untrusted-input production protocol has not been implemented.
No Rust supervisor, hard wall-clock deadline, cancel request, crash recovery, process-tree kill or queue isolation is validated by this probe.
-Xmx512m is a JVM heap bound, not an operating-system total-memory or CPU quota.
Process runs under the current user's permissions; there is no worker sandbox, filesystem allowlist or egress restriction.
Alloy parser can resolve imports; generated-model and pinned-module restrictions remain future work.
Stdout contains one parseable JSON result; Alloy/Kodkod diagnostic logging was observed on stderr and saved separately. Bounded streaming and backpressure remain unimplemented.
No Linux, macOS, ARM or native SAT backend execution was performed. Native directories in the jar are packaging evidence only.
Runtime distribution licenses, dependency SBOM, native library compatibility and portable-JDK release policy require a separate release review.
